topic.source_contract: HMLR corporate title ownership and Companies House identity cross-check

facts.coverage: freehold and leasehold registered titles where the legal owner is a non-private individual
facts.scope_guard: A corporate-title row must be bound to the exact candidate title and site; dataset presence alone is not site identity.

facts.coverage: freehold and leasehold title registrations owned by overseas companies
excluded: UK companies with an overseas address
facts.scope_guard: Dataset absence is not evidence that land has no owner or that no title exists.

dataset_names.ccod: UK companies that own property in England and Wales
dataset_names.ocod: Overseas companies that own property in England and Wales

facts.scope_guard: API availability and dataset naming are not evidence that a candidate join or current title query was executed.

facts.public_information_access: Companies House website and RESTful API
facts.scope_guard: A company record identifies a company and is not a property title, proprietor-site binding or legal boundary.

facts.operations: read public company data and submit authorised changes
facts.scope_guard: Company-name similarity is not used as an ownership join; exact company number and HMLR title relation are required.

scope_guards: CCOD and OCOD rows concern registered corporate title ownership and require exact candidate-title binding.
OCOD exclusions mean dataset absence cannot prove no owner or no registered title.
A title may cover multiple properties and a property may involve multiple title interests.
API availability, access rights and dataset naming do not prove that a current candidate query was executed.
Companies House company records are not HM Land Registry property titles or title polygons.
Company-name similarity is not accepted as an ownership join.
Exact company number, exact HMLR title and exact site relation must be reconciled separately.
No score or promotion is written without current title/register evidence, site binding and executed overlays.
